pageCache.pageTitle: School trips and international experiences - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
School trips and international experiences
Our trips and visits programme is built for breadth. Teachers across the primary and secondary phases take students out to see, hear and do the things that lessons can only describe: a language spoken in the street where it belongs, a landscape they have studied on a map, a gallery, a laboratory, a factory floor, a stage. Each visit extends the curriculum rather than interrupting it.
Just as importantly, trips develop the student. Travelling together builds independence, confidence and the cultural capital that opens doors later on: navigating an unfamiliar place, meeting people whose lives look nothing like your own, and discovering an interest you would never have found in a classroom. Costs and payment dates are published early so families have time to plan, and support is available where cost would otherwise be a barrier.
A sample of recent trips and visits
Kew Gardens, Whipsnade Zoo, climbing at Oakwood, Windsor Castle, Legoland, Heathlands Farm, the Milestone Museum, cooking at Pizza Express, theatre at the Troubadour in Canary Wharf and other theatre trips, Thorpe Park, Geography fieldwork at Hengistbury Head, university and research visits to Oxford Brookes and Southampton, the ski trip, Madrid, Thailand, Nepal and Cambodia, and our performing arts tour to Disney.
This is only a selection. Trips run across every phase, from Key Stage 1 through to KAB6, and the programme changes each year.

pageCache.text:
Careers Programme Information
Preparing Students for Their Futures
At King's Academy Binfield we are incredibly proud of the wide range of opportunities we provide to help students explore their futures. Our careers programme is designed to inspire ambition, develop employability skills and ensure every student understands the many pathways available to them.
From Year 7 through to Sixth Form, students take part in a carefully planned programme of activities that help them discover their strengths, explore career possibilities and make informed decisions about their next steps.
Careers education is woven throughout our curriculum, PSHE programme and enrichment activities so that students regularly encounter employers, workplaces and real-world career pathways.
A High-Quality Careers Programme
Our careers programme is designed in line with the Gatsby Benchmarks, the national framework for best practice in careers education.
These benchmarks ensure that students receive a structured, progressive and meaningful careers programme throughout their time at school. Our approach focuses on:
Providing stable and well-planned careers education from Year 7 to Sixth Form
Linking learning in the classroom to real-world career opportunities
Giving students regular encounters with employers and workplaces
Ensuring access to personalised careers guidance from qualified advisers
Supporting students and parents to understand all progression pathways, including university, apprenticeships and technical education
This approach helps students develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to succeed in their future careers.
Supporting Parents and Carers
Parents and carers play a vital role in helping young people think about their futures. Conversations at home about interests, ambitions and opportunities can have a powerful impact on students’ confidence and decision-making.
To help families feel informed and supported, we provide regular opportunities for parents to engage with our careers programme. These include information evenings, webinars, options events and post-16 guidance sessions, where parents can learn more about the different pathways available to their children.
We also encourage parents to create a parent account on Unifrog, our online careers platform. This allows parents to explore the same information that students use in school and to support discussions at home about future pathways.
By signing up to Unifrog, parents can:
Explore university, apprenticeship and college options
Understand the range of career pathways available after school
Access up-to-date labour market information
Support their child with researching careers and progression routes
Learn more about application processes and key decision points
Working in partnership with parents ensures that every student receives consistent guidance and encouragement both in school and at home.
If you would like help setting up your parent account or accessing careers information, please contact our Careers Leader (careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk,) who will be happy to help.
Careers Support from Employers
We are keen to work with businesses, employers, universities and training providers to help our students understand the opportunities open to them, both locally in Berkshire and the Thames Valley and nationally. This work links directly to Gatsby Benchmark 5, encounters with employers and employees, and Gatsby Benchmark 6, experiences of workplaces.
Employer involvement is one of the things students remember longest. A single conversation with someone who does the job can change what a young person believes is possible for them. If you are willing to give some time, we would be glad to hear from you.
Year 10 students complete a week of work experience in May. Year 12 students complete a week of work experience at a point in the academic year that suits their placement, which gives them the flexibility to secure something with an employer they have a genuine interest in rather than being tied to a fixed week.
Work experience gives students real insight into the day to day reality of a role and an organisation, and lets them see the skills they have been building in the classroom applied in a working environment. We are always looking for employers able to host a student.
Year 10 students take part in a Mock Interview Day. Students attend in formal dress and are interviewed by industry professionals, who ask a range of interview questions, give feedback on how the student performed, and offer practical advice on how to improve.
For many students this is the first interview they have ever had. Volunteer interviewers make this possible, and no specialist training is needed. We provide the questions, the structure and the feedback forms.
Our Careers Fair brings employers, universities, colleges and training providers into the academy to talk directly to students about their industries and the routes into them. Exhibitors need only a table and a willingness to answer questions.
If you would rather talk to students about your industry and your own route into it, we can arrange this in whatever format suits you:
A fifteen minute assembly to a whole year group.
We are particularly interested in hearing from people whose route was not a straight line, and from those working in industries our students may not have considered.
We are especially keen to find mentors willing to work with our students with special educational needs and disabilities. These young people often face the greatest barriers in finding and sustaining employment, and mentoring, work shadowing and supported placements can open doors in a genuinely meaningful way.
No prior experience is needed. We will provide information and support, and you will be making a real and lasting difference to a young person's prospects.
If you would like to support our careers programme in any of these ways, please contact careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk and we will be in touch to discuss what would work best for you and for our students.
Our provider access policy statement, setting out how providers of technical education and apprenticeships can request access to speak to our students, is available to download below.
Useful Careers Resources and Websites
A huge amount of careers information is available online. The sites below are a good starting point for students and for parents and carers supporting conversations at home. If you cannot find what you need, please contact the careers team.
Unifrog is the platform every KAB student has an account for, bringing career profiles, apprenticeship vacancies, college and university courses and application tools together in one place. Parents and carers can create a linked account.
Bracknell Forest Information, Advice and Support Service gives free, confidential and impartial advice to children, young people and families on SEND, including EHCP applications, reviews and appeals. It is a self referral service and no diagnosis or plan is needed. Contact iass@bracknell-forest.gov.uk
Elevate Bracknell Forest provides careers guidance to young people up to 25 who are care leavers or have an EHCP, as well as to those at risk of becoming NEET.
Find an apprenticeship is the government service for searching and applying.
GetMyFirstJob lists apprenticeships and entry level roles.

pageCache.text:
Apprenticeships
What is an apprenticeship?
An apprenticeship is a genuine job with training attached. Apprentices are employed, paid a wage and given time to study, which means they gain a recognised qualification without taking on tuition fee debt. Apprenticeships are not a fallback for students who cannot go to university. Many are highly competitive, and they are offered by some of the largest and most prestigious employers in the country.
The levels explained
How we support students
Apprenticeships are covered explicitly in our PSHE and Personal Development curriculum, at the options stage in Year 9, and again during post-16 and post-18 planning. Students can research apprenticeship standards, employers and vacancies through Unifrog, and every student can request a one to one guidance appointment with our independent careers adviser, Mr Tim Swithenbank, to talk through whether an apprenticeship is the right route for them.
We also welcome apprenticeship providers and employers into the academy to speak directly to students, as set out in our provider access policy statement.
Where to search and apply
Please note that many large employers advertise apprenticeships on their own websites and recruit early, often in the autumn term. Students should not wait until the summer to start looking.
Applying and interviewing
Most apprenticeship applications require a CV and a covering letter, and almost all involve an interview. Mr Tim Swithenbank and the careers team can help students prepare both, and we run mock interviews as part of our careers programme.

pageCache.pageTitle: Higher Education Preparation - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
Higher Education Preparation
Higher education is one of several routes open to students when they leave King's Academy Binfield, alongside apprenticeships, employment and further training. Students who choose any of these routes get the same support from us.
This page explains how we prepare students for university and other higher education, what happens and when, and where families can find reliable information.
What counts as higher education
Higher education covers qualifications at level 4 and above, usually studied after A levels:
Bachelor's degrees, normally three years full time
Students can study full time or part time, live at home or move away, and start straight after Year 13 or later.
How we prepare students
Key Stage 4 Careers lessons cover the routes available after Year 11 and where each one leads. Year 10 students attend university taster days, and every student has a one-to-one meeting with our independent careers adviser during Year 11.
Year 12 Students take part in the KS5 enrichment programme covering career routes, applications, CVs and interview skills. They attend the Newbury Destinations Expo, the KAB Careers Fair, a visit to the University of Oxford and the UCAS trip, and are given time to attend open days of their own choosing. Student Finance and University Costs is taught so that money is understood before choices are made. Students also complete work experience and have one-to-one careers guidance meetings.
Year 13 Applications and Deadlines is taught at the start of the autumn term, covering post-18 choices, personal statements, references and predicted grades. Students draft and redraft their personal statements with subject teachers and tutors, have further careers guidance meetings, and receive support with interviews and admissions tests where a course requires them.
Key dates
Most applications to UK universities are made through UCAS. The academy manages references and submission, so students apply through us rather than directly.
Year 12, spring and summer
Research courses, attend open days, start thinking about the personal statement
UCAS accounts set up; first drafts of personal statements
UCAS deadline of 15 October for Oxford and Cambridge, and for medicine, dentistry and veterinary courses
Year 13, October to December
Statements finalised, references written, applications checked and submitted
UCAS equal consideration deadline
Offers, interviews and applicant days; firm and insurance choices; student finance applications
Results day, confirmation of places, and support with Clearing where needed
Our internal deadlines are earlier than the UCAS deadlines, so that references can be written and applications checked properly. Students are given these dates in September.
Choosing a course
We encourage students to choose the course first and the place second. Useful questions:
What is actually taught on this course, and how is it assessed? Two courses with the same title can be very different
Students should attend at least two open days before they apply. Open days are the single most useful thing a student can do.
Personal statements
The personal statement is the student's own account of why they want to study the subject and what they have done to explore it. Universities look for evidence: wider reading, lectures and online courses, work experience, volunteering, part-time work, and what the student learned from each. Reflection matters more than a list of activities.
Statements are drafted in tutor time and subject lessons, reviewed by subject specialists and redrafted several times. They must be the student's own work. Universities check for plagiarism and for text generated by artificial intelligence.
References are written by the academy and include predicted grades agreed by subject teachers, based on assessment evidence.
Courses that need earlier preparation
Some courses need work starting in Year 12, not Year 13:
Oxford and Cambridge: UCAS deadline of 15 October, admissions tests and written work in most subjects, interviews in December
Students considering any of these should speak to the Careers Leader or their tutor during Year 12.
Paying for university
Cost should inform decisions but should not rule higher education out. Full-time undergraduates in England can usually apply for:
A tuition fee loan, paid directly to the university, so students never have to find fees up front
Repayment begins only once a graduate earns above a threshold, is taken automatically through the payroll, and stops if earnings fall below it. Rates and thresholds change, so please check current figures on gov.uk student finance rather than relying on what was true for an older sibling.
Student finance applications open in the spring of Year 13 and should be submitted before the deadline, even if a place is not yet confirmed.
Degree apprenticeships
A degree apprenticeship combines paid employment with study for a full degree. The employer pays the tuition, so there are no fees and no student loan. Competition is often higher than for the equivalent degree, and applications are made directly to employers, with their own deadlines through the autumn and spring.
Students can apply for degree apprenticeships and through UCAS at the same time, and we encourage strong candidates to do both.
Our Apprenticeships page has more detail for students and parents, including how apprenticeships work at each level, where to search for vacancies and how the application process differs from UCAS.
Students who will be the first in their family to apply
Nobody is expected to already understand the system. We offer step-by-step support through every stage, access to university outreach programmes for students without a family history of higher education, campus visits, and contact with former students who have made the same step from King's Academy Binfield.
Students with SEND
Students with SEND are supported to apply on the same terms as their peers. This includes identifying universities with strong support, applying for Disabled Students' Allowance, planning visits with additional support, and discussing next steps at every annual review of an education, health and care plan. Our SENCO and Careers Leader work together on this from Year 12.
How parents and carers can help
Go to open days together where you can
Ask about the course, not just the university name or league table position
Results day
Staff are on site on results day in August, and students can collect their results in person and speak to the sixth form team and the Careers Leader. If grades meet the firm offer, the place is confirmed automatically. If not, the insurance choice may be confirmed, or we support students through Clearing. Students who do better than expected can look at Adjustment. Students who decide university is not for them are supported into apprenticeships, employment or training.
Nobody leaves without a plan, and we continue to support students after they have left if their plans change.
Helpful resources
Researching courses and universities
UCAS — all higher education course applications are made through UCAS
Open days and taster days
Who to contact
Mrs L Newhouse, Careers Leader careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk 01344 306983

pageCache.pageTitle: Labour Market Information - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
Labour Market Information
What is labour market information?
Labour market information, usually shortened to LMI, is information about the world of work. It describes what different jobs involve, what qualifications and skills they need, how much they typically pay, how many people do them, where those jobs are, and whether the number of them is growing or shrinking.
Put simply, LMI answers the question: what does this career actually look like, and what will it look like by the time I get there?
Why it matters
Most students pick a career from the small number of jobs they have seen: the jobs their family do, the jobs they see in their town, and the jobs that appear on television. LMI widens that picture.
Good LMI helps students to:
It matters for parents and carers too. Families are one of the biggest influences on the choices young people make, and the jobs market today looks very different from the one most of us entered.
Discover jobs they had never heard of
Challenge assumptions about who does which job
Questions LMI can answer
What do people actually do in this job?
What qualifications and skills do I need?
How we use LMI at King's Academy Binfield
LMI is built into our careers programme rather than left for students to find on their own.
Years 7 to 9: careers lessons introduce the world of work, employment rights and working patterns, and students begin using Unifrog to research jobs and sectors. Employer assemblies and events such as STEM Day.
The job market where we live
Bracknell Forest sits in the Thames Valley, one of the strongest local economies in the country and an area with an unusually high concentration of technology, digital and business services employers. Many large companies have UK or European headquarters within a short distance of the academy, and several work with us directly on careers activities.
That means our students have local access to careers in areas including:
Students should not feel limited to local jobs, and many will move away to study or work. But it is worth knowing what is on the doorstep, particularly for apprenticeships, which are usually taken with a local employer.
Education and childcare
Construction, engineering and the skilled trades
Retail, hospitality, logistics and distribution
Priority sectors for growth
The government has identified eight sectors expected to drive economic growth over the coming years:
Advanced manufacturing
We make sure students meet employers from across a range of these sectors during their time with us.
Clean energy industries
Creative industries
Digital and technologies
Financial services
Life sciences
Professional and business services
Things to keep in mind when using LMI
Averages hide a lot. Advertised pay for a job varies enormously by employer, region and experience. Starting salaries are usually well below the average figure quoted.
Pay is not the only measure. Hours, job security, travel, progression and whether you would enjoy the work all matter.
Tools for exploring LMI
Careerometer — compare up to three jobs side by side on pay, working hours and future employment prospects
Skillsometer — for students who are not yet sure what interests them; a short quiz that suggests jobs based on what they enjoy
Find an apprenticeship — search live apprenticeship vacancies by area and sector to see what local employers are recruiting for
Discover Uni — official data on degree courses, including what graduates go on to earn and do
For parents and carers
You do not need to be an expert to have a useful conversation about careers. The most helpful things you can do are to stay curious, keep options open, and use current information rather than what was true when you left school.
Look at a job profile together on the National Careers Service and talk about what surprises you
Who to contact
Mrs L Newhouse, Careers Leader careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk 01344 306983

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Programme Information - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
Careers Programme Information
Preparing Students for Their Futures
At King's Academy Binfield we are incredibly proud of the wide range of opportunities we provide to help students explore their futures. Our careers programme is designed to inspire ambition, develop employability skills and ensure every student understands the many pathways available to them.
From Year 7 through to Sixth Form, students take part in a carefully planned programme of activities that help them discover their strengths, explore career possibilities and make informed decisions about their next steps.
Careers education is woven throughout our curriculum, PSHE programme and enrichment activities so that students regularly encounter employers, workplaces and real-world career pathways.
A High-Quality Careers Programme
Our careers programme is designed in line with the Gatsby Benchmarks, the national framework for best practice in careers education.
These benchmarks ensure that students receive a structured, progressive and meaningful careers programme throughout their time at school. Our approach focuses on:
Providing stable and well-planned careers education from Year 7 to Sixth Form
Linking learning in the classroom to real-world career opportunities
Giving students regular encounters with employers and workplaces
Ensuring access to personalised careers guidance from qualified advisers
Supporting students and parents to understand all progression pathways, including university, apprenticeships and technical education
This approach helps students develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to succeed in their future careers.
Supporting Parents and Carers
Parents and carers play a vital role in helping young people think about their futures. Conversations at home about interests, ambitions and opportunities can have a powerful impact on students’ confidence and decision-making.
To help families feel informed and supported, we provide regular opportunities for parents to engage with our careers programme. These include information evenings, webinars, options events and post-16 guidance sessions, where parents can learn more about the different pathways available to their children.
We also encourage parents to create a parent account on Unifrog, our online careers platform. This allows parents to explore the same information that students use in school and to support discussions at home about future pathways.
By signing up to Unifrog, parents can:
Explore university, apprenticeship and college options
Understand the range of career pathways available after school
Access up-to-date labour market information
Support their child with researching careers and progression routes
Learn more about application processes and key decision points
Working in partnership with parents ensures that every student receives consistent guidance and encouragement both in school and at home.
If you would like help setting up your parent account or accessing careers information, please contact our Careers Leader (careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk,) who will be happy to help.
Careers Support from Employers
We are keen to work with businesses, employers, universities and training providers to help our students understand the opportunities open to them, both locally in Berkshire and the Thames Valley and nationally. This work links directly to Gatsby Benchmark 5, encounters with employers and employees, and Gatsby Benchmark 6, experiences of workplaces.
Employer involvement is one of the things students remember longest. A single conversation with someone who does the job can change what a young person believes is possible for them. If you are willing to give some time, we would be glad to hear from you.
Year 10 students complete a week of work experience in May. Year 12 students complete a week of work experience at a point in the academic year that suits their placement, which gives them the flexibility to secure something with an employer they have a genuine interest in rather than being tied to a fixed week.
Work experience gives students real insight into the day to day reality of a role and an organisation, and lets them see the skills they have been building in the classroom applied in a working environment. We are always looking for employers able to host a student.
Year 10 students take part in a Mock Interview Day. Students attend in formal dress and are interviewed by industry professionals, who ask a range of interview questions, give feedback on how the student performed, and offer practical advice on how to improve.
For many students this is the first interview they have ever had. Volunteer interviewers make this possible, and no specialist training is needed. We provide the questions, the structure and the feedback forms.
Our Careers Fair brings employers, universities, colleges and training providers into the academy to talk directly to students about their industries and the routes into them. Exhibitors need only a table and a willingness to answer questions.
If you would rather talk to students about your industry and your own route into it, we can arrange this in whatever format suits you:
A fifteen minute assembly to a whole year group.
We are particularly interested in hearing from people whose route was not a straight line, and from those working in industries our students may not have considered.
We are especially keen to find mentors willing to work with our students with special educational needs and disabilities. These young people often face the greatest barriers in finding and sustaining employment, and mentoring, work shadowing and supported placements can open doors in a genuinely meaningful way.
No prior experience is needed. We will provide information and support, and you will be making a real and lasting difference to a young person's prospects.
If you would like to support our careers programme in any of these ways, please contact careers.bi@kingsacademies.uk and we will be in touch to discuss what would work best for you and for our students.
Our provider access policy statement, setting out how providers of technical education and apprenticeships can request access to speak to our students, is available to download below.
Useful Careers Resources and Websites
A huge amount of careers information is available online. The sites below are a good starting point for students and for parents and carers supporting conversations at home. If you cannot find what you need, please contact the careers team.
Unifrog is the platform every KAB student has an account for, bringing career profiles, apprenticeship vacancies, college and university courses and application tools together in one place. Parents and carers can create a linked account.
Bracknell Forest Information, Advice and Support Service gives free, confidential and impartial advice to children, young people and families on SEND, including EHCP applications, reviews and appeals. It is a self referral service and no diagnosis or plan is needed. Contact iass@bracknell-forest.gov.uk
Elevate Bracknell Forest provides careers guidance to young people up to 25 who are care leavers or have an EHCP, as well as to those at risk of becoming NEET.
Find an apprenticeship is the government service for searching and applying.
GetMyFirstJob lists apprenticeships and entry level roles.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra Curricular, Trips & Activities - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular, Trips & Activities
We place great emphasis on learning beyond the classroom and take every opportunity to get our students out into the real world. Enrichment is not an add-on at KAB: it sits at the heart of our Personal Development programme, alongside PSHE, careers education and tutor time, and it is how students discover what they are good at, what they care about, and who they want to become.
Students are encouraged to join clubs and societies that run before school, during lunchtime and after school. Performing Arts and PE are our two largest extra-curricular departments, and between them they account for a great deal of what happens at KAB outside lesson time. Our performing arts companies rehearse and perform throughout the year, instrumental and vocal lessons are taught to a large number of students, teams train and play fixtures through the season, and each year students travel with us locally, nationally and internationally. All of it is built around our KGA values of Honesty, Faith and Courage.
Student Leaders & School Council
The School Council is how students have a formal say in how the academy runs. Representatives are elected by their tutor groups from every year, and the council meets once a fortnight. Meetings are led by our Head Team, with a member of staff there to facilitate: students set the agenda, chair the meeting and carry the actions, and staff make sure the right people hear about it and come back with an answer.
Items come straight from tutor time discussions and from students approaching their representative, so the agenda is genuinely theirs: the clubs and trips students want to see, facilities and the school environment, uniform and catering, charity choices, and how the academy responds to things that are not working. Representatives report back to their tutor groups after each meeting so everyone can see what happened to their suggestion, and the Head Team follows items up with the lead member of staff between meetings. Where the council asks for something we cannot do, we explain why.
Much of our enrichment offer has been shaped this way, and student voice is one of the main things we use to decide what to run next year.
Leadership at KAB is something students do, not a badge they are given. These roles are open across the year groups and each is supported by a member of staff.
A great deal of valuable work happens outside lesson time. Clubs run through the lunch hour and after school, led by our own staff and by visiting coaches and specialists.
Homework Club is open Monday - Thursday and is supervised by a member of staff, giving students a quiet, supported place to work with access to Chromebooks and printing. Please register on Arbor.
Clubs for the Autumn Term 2026 will be confirmed in the coming weeks. The full timetable will be published on this page and shared with students in tutor time.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Duke of Edinburgh's Award - Kings Academy Binfield
pageCache.text:
The Duke of Edinburgh's Award
The Duke of Edinburgh's Award is a non-competitive, internationally recognised programme that encourages young people to develop new skills and take on new challenges. It is open to all students.
The award helps young people gain the skills they need to navigate adult life: independence, teamwork, problem solving, resilience, confidence, respect for their community and an appreciation of their environment. It is highly regarded by employers and universities, and for many students it is the experience they remember most from their time at school.
Students log their own progress through the eDofE system and are supported at school by our DofE team, with training sessions and practice expeditions before each qualifying trip.
Where every student starts, with no experience needed. Participants choose their own activities across three sections and keep them going for at least three months each, with one section carried on for six months.
Volunteering — giving time to help other people or a cause
Available in Year 10 and Year 12 to students who have completed their Bronze. The same sections, but sustained for longer: six months of volunteering and six months on one of the other two, with the remaining section running for at least three months.
